articles.title: Long-term Survivorship of Transfibular Trabecular Metal Total Ankle Arthroplasty: 10-Year Minimum Clinical and Radiographic Follow-up.
articles.authors: Schafer KA, Day J, Convery K, Zhang Z, Schon LC
articles.study_type: Retrospective case series with prospective follow-up
articles.population: Patients with ankle arthritis who underwent primary transfibular total ankle arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Implant survivorship, patient-reported outcomes (pain, function, quality of life), radiographic alignment and motion, reoperations, periprosthetic lucencies
articles.take_home: After 11 years, the trabecular metal ankle replacement had a 98.6% survival rate with stable function and alignment, though 41% of patients needed minor follow-up procedures such as scar tissue removal. The implant appears durable as a long-term treatment for ankle arthritis.

articles.title: Preoperative Computer Simulation and 3D-Printed Guide Plate of Autologous Transplantation Achieved Favorable Outcomes in Patients With Large Cystic Osteochondral Lesion of the Talus.
articles.authors: Cai B, Cheng X, Su T, Hu Y, Guo Q, Jiao C, et al.
articles.population: Patients with large cystic osteochondral lesions of the talus (bone in the ankle)
articles.sample_size: 32 patients (19 conventional surgery, 13 with computer-planned surgery)
articles.outcomes: Pain scores, daily function scores, surgery time, cyst recurrence, postoperative complications
articles.take_home: Using computer simulation and 3D-printed surgical guides for ankle bone graft surgery resulted in less pain, better daily function, shorter operating time, and lower rates of the cyst coming back compared to conventional surgery. However, the study was small and non-randomised, so these results need confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: No Difference in Short-term Postoperative Complication Rates Between Non-chilled and Chilled Saline Irrigation in Percutaneous Foot and Ankle Surgery.
articles.authors: Fiore PI, Gonzalez TA, Montagna A, Johnson AH, Vulcano E
articles.population: Patients undergoing percutaneous double osteotomy bunionectomy
articles.outcomes: Union rates, time to union, postoperative complication rates
articles.take_home: Using chilled saline instead of non-chilled saline during foot surgery did not reduce complications or speed up bone healing. Both groups had excellent healing rates and similarly low complication rates.

articles.title: Postoperative hindfoot alignment after sinus tarsi versus extensile lateral approach for Sanders type III-IV calcaneal fractures.
articles.authors: Yavuz U, Buyukkuscu MO, Kocabiyik A, Tuncer S, Polat A, Guler M
articles.population: Patients with Sanders type III-IV intra-articular calcaneal fractures
articles.sample_size: 74 patients (36 extensile lateral approach, 38 sinus tarsi approach)
articles.outcomes: Postoperative hindfoot alignment angle, calcaneal width, Bohler and Gissane angles, AOFAS score, VAS pain score
articles.take_home: Both surgical approaches produced similar results for complex heel fractures in terms of alignment, X-ray findings and pain relief. The less invasive sinus tarsi approach may be a reasonable alternative to the more extensive surgical approach.

articles.title: Ligament Advanced Reinforcement System (LARS) Augmented Repair vs Autograft Reconstruction for Chronic Lateral Ankle Instability: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
articles.authors: Wu T, Li Z, Zhao J, Hao C, Xie W, Fu K, et al.
articles.population: Adults with chronic lateral ankle instability
articles.sample_size: 112 patients (54 LARS augmented repair, 58 autograft reconstruction)
articles.outcomes: Foot and Ankle Outcome Score Sport subscale, Tegner activity score, pain scores, functional recovery trajectory over 24 months
articles.take_home: Both surgical techniques improved ankle function significantly over 2 years. LARS augmented repair patients recovered faster in the first 6 months, but by 12 months and beyond, both groups had similar functional outcomes.

articles.title: Outcomes of AO/OTA 43C Pilon Fractures Treated With Open Reduction Internal Fixation or Tibiotalocalcaneal Nailing.
articles.authors: Litten RM, Sankey MT, Harris CS, McIlwain RN, Spitler CA, Johnson JP, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years or older with severe ankle fractures (AO/OTA 43C pilon fractures) treated with surgery
articles.sample_size: 436 patients in unmatched cohort; 70 matched pairs (140 total in matched analysis)
articles.outcomes: Fracture-related infection, need for further surgery, fracture nonunion, amputation, and hospital length of stay
articles.take_home: Two different surgical approaches (tibiotalocalcaneal nailing and open reduction internal fixation) produced similar rates of infection, reoperation, nonunion and amputation for severe ankle fractures. Tibiotalocalcaneal nailing can be considered an effective treatment option, particularly in complex cases.

articles.title: Functional Outcomes Following Hallux Sesamoidectomy in Athletic and Non-Athletic Populations at Two-Year Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Austin WP, Saggar R, Mullen JP, Olawin AO, Williams A, Heidinger E, et al.
articles.population: Patients with hallux sesamoid pathology that did not improve with conservative treatment, including both athletes and non-athletes
articles.outcomes: Pain scores (visual analog scale), daily living function (FAAM ADL), sports function (FAAM Sports), and physical and mental health scores measured at average 2.3 years after surgery
articles.take_home: Patients who had their hallux sesamoid bone removed experienced meaningful pain relief and improved function in daily activities and sports at two-year follow-up. Athletes in particular showed significant improvement in their ability to participate in sports.

articles.title: Radiofrequency Ablation for Interdigital Neuroma: Moderate 2-Year Outcomes and Surgical Conversion Rate.
articles.authors: Diaz-Fernandez R, Martin-de-Salvador P, Valverde-Vazquez R, Oliver-Grosso A
articles.population: Patients with a single symptomatic interdigital neuroma
articles.outcomes: Pain relief measured by visual analog scale (VAS) and functional improvement measured by Manchester-Oxford Foot Questionnaire (MOXFQ); rate of subsequent surgery needed
articles.take_home: Radiofrequency ablation provided meaningful pain relief in about two-thirds of patients and improved function in most patients over 2 years, but around one-quarter of patients eventually needed conventional surgery. It appears to be a reasonable option to try before surgery, though patients should be prepared that it may not be a permanent fix.

articles.title: Offloading strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Koonalinthip P, Koonalintip P, Koonalinthip N
articles.study_type: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
articles.take_home: Surgical offloading and non-removable knee-high devices (both custom-made and standard) were more effective at healing diabetic foot ulcers compared to usual care. Surgical offloading may be a good option for some patients alongside these non-removable devices.

articles.title: Impact of BMI on two-year clinical outcomes following surgical treatment of insertional achilles tendinopathy.
articles.authors: Tan YJ, Tay AYW, Mohamed Buhary KS, Toh RX, Li ZX, Tay KS
articles.population: Patients undergoing surgical treatment for insertional Achilles tendinopathy
articles.outcomes: AOFAS hindfoot score, pain (VAS), SF-36 physical and mental scores, patient satisfaction, wound complications at 2 years
articles.take_home: Patients with obesity achieved similar improvements in pain, function and satisfaction after Achilles tendon surgery as those with normal weight, suggesting BMI does not prevent good surgical outcomes. Wound complications were slightly higher in obese patients but the difference was not statistically significant.

articles.title: Dynamic ultrasound (DUS) versus magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for the diagnosis of Morton's neuroma: A prospective comparative study.
articles.authors: Biz C, Crimi F, Sciarretta G, Crimi A, Dimaggio A, Corso A, et al.
articles.sample_size: 76 lesions (53 Morton's neuromas, 23 intermetatarsal bursitis cases)
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of dynamic ultrasound versus MRI; dynamic ultrasound achieved 98.68% accuracy compared to MRI's 89.47%
articles.take_home: Dynamic ultrasound was more accurate than MRI for diagnosing Morton's neuroma and may be a better first-line imaging test. It is also more cost-effective than MRI.

articles.title: Subtalar joint dynamics in progressive collapsing foot deformity: A cross-sectional progression model.
articles.authors: Vermorel PH, Lintz F, Pozzessere E, Luo E, Easley M, Grun W, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cross-sectional study using imaging analysis
articles.population: Patients with progressive collapsing foot deformity at different stages
articles.outcomes: Three-dimensional measurements of talar position, subluxation, incongruence, and various joint offsets across four stages of deformity progression
articles.take_home: The study found that progressive collapsing foot deformity develops in stages: it starts with the talus rotating inward relative to the foot, then worsens with the talus shifting inward and the subtalar joint opening outward, before finally progressing with the centre of collapse moving toward the outer part of the talus.

articles.title: Accessibility of the talus through an anterior arthrotomy for treatment of osteochondral lesions using autologous matrix-induced chondrogenesis.
articles.authors: Ivanova S, Bieri Y, Krause F, Lustenberger T, Anwander H
articles.population: Patients undergoing autologous matrix-induced chondrogenesis for osteochondral lesions of the talus
articles.outcomes: Proportion of cases requiring malleolar osteotomy based on lesion location; sensitivity and specificity of location-based prediction
articles.take_home: Lesions in the front three quarters of the ankle bone can usually be treated without cutting the ankle bone, but lesions extending towards the back are more likely to need this extra surgery. The location of the lesion on imaging can help predict whether osteotomy will be needed.
